newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to introduce pollution controls.
newsitem.headline: Canada to introduce pollution controls.

text.p: Canada is set to introduce an enhanced Canadian Environmental Protection Act on Tuesday, but environmentalists voiced concern the bill would not adequately deal with pollution problems.

The legislation would establish improved "whistle-blower" protection to encourage Canadians to report environmental violations, and create wide-ranging enforcement powers to crack down on polluters by expanding powers for inspectors.
The bill would also introduce new safety regulations for the use of biotechnology products.
Environment Minister Sergio Marchi announced on Monday he would be introducing the bill in Parliament the following day.

Some environmentalists said the bill, a draft of which was obtained by Reuters, was watered down. They want the government to follow the 140 recommendations made by the Standing Committee on Environment and Sustainable Development in June 1995, which would have completely revamped the act.

"The legislation will be a far cry from the standing committee's recommendations," Paul Muldoon, a lawyer for the Canadian Environmental Law Association, told Reuters. "It will not take a tough stand on toxic chemicals and in fact we are fearful it limits the government from acting in some areas."

First passed in 1988, the original law deals with pollution and waste on land, water and air. The new bill covers issues ranging from vehicle emissions and genetic engineering to environmental matters related to regulations.
